stances_toward.note: The PKK is a foreign armed group on Iraqi soil that draws Turkish bombing and keeps Turkish bases in the north; Baghdad wants it gone and wants the Turkish forces gone with it, but is not at war with it. Warming because the dissolution process is working: the PKK said on 16 November 2025 it had left the Zap region, Turkey's parliament passed Law No. 7595 on 10 August 2026, and Turkey agreed to hand over Bashiqa on 24 September; an unidentified drone still killed a PKK member in Sulaymaniyah on 19 July 2025. Al-Zaidi's roadmap includes disarming 'all non-Iraqi armed groups'. Our reading; no source uses the word rival. Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: The matrix: the YPG and PYD grew out of the Ocalan movement (Abdi trained with the PKK in Iraq in the early 1990s and returned to Syria in 2011), which is why Ankara equates the two; the SDF has always claimed a separate Syrian command. The PKK's dissolution (12 May 2025, after Ocalan's call of 27 Feb) and Turkey's peace law of 10 Aug 2026 end the shared war; the 18 Jan 2026 deal required the SDF to expel non-Syrian PKK-affiliated members, which Abdi said on 20 Aug 2026 was done; on 18 Sep 2026 the KCK's Cemil Bayik criticised Abdi for taking a state post. Graded `partner`, not `ally`: lineage and ideology without a shared command today; cooling. The PKK card is a stub: no stance of its own toward the SDF yet. Grade C, our reading. Bond - kin.

relations_to.summary: 27 Feb 2025: Ocalan calls on the PKK to hold a congress, disarm and dissolve; the PKK declares a ceasefire (1 Mar), and its 12th congress (5-7 May, Suleymaniyah and Duhok) announces on 12 May the dissolution and an end to all military and political activity in Iraq, Iran, Syria and Turkey. Turkey's peace process then passes Law No. 7595 (10 Aug 2026). The SDF's relation to the decision is not settled: Ankara demanded the SDF follow, and the 18 Jan 2026 deal required it to expel non-Syrian PKK-affiliated members.
